title: 1. Wall geometry and exposed faces
text: Each cheek wall stands on the pier cap top at the cap end (3 in in from the end), full cap width, with a shallow recessed panel on its outside face. The wall is a vertical cantilever fixed at the cap top; the panel reduces the thickness over the middle of the height, so two sections are checked: A at the cap top and B at the panel bottom.

title: 2. Design wind pressure
text: The pressure of LRFD Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-1 with the substructure drag coefficient, as the direct pier wind of C002: the Strength III speed and exposure coefficient of C001, the Strength V and Service I speeds of LRFD Table 3.8.1.1.2-1 with K_Z = 1.0, and the gust factor of SDG 2.4.1.C. The wind load factor is 1.0 in all three combinations (LRFD Table 3.4.1-1), so the largest strength pressure governs.

title: 3. Direct wind delivered to the pier
text: LRFD 3.8.1.2.3b applies the pressure to the exposed substructure areas seen in end and front elevation. Each wall adds its broad face to the pier's transverse area and its edge to the longitudinal area; the resultants act at mid-height above the cap top. The wall itself is designed for the full pressure normal to its face, which bounds the face component of every skewed wind direction.

title: 4. Wall demands as a cantilever from the cap top
text: The pressure on the whole face is a uniform line load up the wall; the base shear and the moments at sections A and B follow. Self-weight compression is neglected (conservative for flexure and interface shear). No fill, bearing or superstructure contact loads the wall.

title: 5. Materials, bars and section constants
text: Concrete and reinforcement properties of the pier cap case; the bar sizes of the mat.

title: 6. Section A at the cap top (full thickness)
text: Rectangular section of the full wall width with the single layer of verticals. Wind can act on either face, so the effective depth is the lesser of the bar's distances to the two faces. Flexure (LRFD 5.6.3.2), minimum reinforcement (5.6.3.3), crack control (5.6.7, applied only where the service tension exceeds 0.8 fr), the SDG service stress limit and shear (5.7.3.3 with the simplified β) are evaluated.

title: 7. Section B at the bottom of the recessed panel
text: The same section checks on the net thickness behind the panel, with the smaller moment of the wind above the panel bottom. Compression on the recessed face gives the smaller effective depth.

title: 8. Development of the verticals into the cap
text: The verticals run straight into the cap. LRFD 5.10.8.2.1a gives the basic length, 5.10.8.2.1c the confinement factor from the cover in the cap (no transverse steel credited) and the excess reinforcement factor from the steel the minimum design moment requires; the result is not less than 12 in.

title: 9. Interface shear at the construction joint
text: Shear friction across the cap top with the SDG 1.15 clean-joint factors and no permanent compression; the verticals are the interface reinforcement.

title: 10. Distribution steel, spacing, cover and thickness
text: Shrinkage and temperature steel of LRFD 5.10.6 (both face requirements carried by the one centred mat), the maximum spacing of primary and distribution steel, the minimum clear spacing, the SDG cover for cheek walls and the SDM minimum thickness.

title: 11. Demand-to-capacity ratios
text: Every check as a ratio of demand to capacity, or of required to provided; the register lists them with their status.
